topics.label: The Moon's Orbit and Tides
facts: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite, and it takes about 27 days to travel around Earth.
The Moon's gravity pulls on Earth's oceans and causes the tides.
The Moon has no air and no weather, so footprints left by astronauts stay there for a very long time.
The same side of the Moon always faces Earth.

questions.q: How long does the Moon take to travel around Earth?
questions.fact: The Moon orbits Earth once in about 27 days.

questions.q: What does the Moon's gravity cause on Earth?
questions.fact: The Moon's gravity pulls ocean water, making high and low tides.

questions.q: Why do astronauts' footprints stay on the Moon for so long?
choices: There is no air or weather to wash them away
The Moon is made of glue
questions.fact: With no wind or rain, footprints on the Moon can last millions of years.

questions.q: Which side of the Moon do we always see from Earth?
questions.fact: The Moon spins at the same speed as it orbits, so the same side always faces us.

topics.label: Earth's Tilt and the Seasons
facts: Seasons happen because Earth's axis is tilted as it travels around the Sun.
When your part of Earth tilts towards the Sun, you get summer; when it tilts away, you get winter.
At the North Pole, the Sun can stay up for months in summer and stay down for months in winter.
Spring and autumn happen when Earth is tilted neither towards nor away from the Sun.

choices: Earth's tilted axis as it orbits the Sun
The Sun getting bigger and smaller
questions.fact: Earth's axis is tilted, so different parts get more or less sunlight through the year.

questions.q: When your part of Earth tilts towards the Sun, which season is it?
questions.fact: Tilting towards the Sun gives longer days and warmer weather: summer.

questions.q: How long does Earth take to travel once around the Sun?
questions.fact: Earth's trip around the Sun takes about 365 days, which is one year.

questions.q: Which season comes between summer and winter?
questions.fact: Autumn comes after summer, when leaves fall and days get shorter.

topics.label: Weather Systems
facts: Weather is driven by the Sun heating Earth's air and water unevenly.
Warm air rises and cool air sinks, and this movement makes wind.
High-pressure areas usually bring calm, clear weather, while low-pressure areas often bring clouds and rain.
Meteorologists use satellites, radar, and weather stations to forecast the weather.

choices: The Sun heating air and water unevenly
questions.fact: Uneven heating by the Sun makes air move, which creates wind and weather.
Warm air is lighter, so it rises, while cool air sinks.

questions.q: Which kind of pressure area usually brings clear, calm weather?
questions.fact: High-pressure air sinks and usually brings settled, clear weather.
Meteorologists study the atmosphere and predict the weather.

topics.label: Eclipses
facts: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes between Earth and the Sun and blocks the Sun's light.
A lunar eclipse happens when Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon, and Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.
During a total solar eclipse, the sky goes dark in the middle of the day for a few minutes.
You must never look straight at the Sun during a solar eclipse without special eclipse glasses.

questions.q: What happens during a solar eclipse?
choices: The Moon passes between Earth and the Sun
Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon
questions.fact: In a solar eclipse, the Moon blocks the Sun's light from reaching Earth.

questions.q: What happens during a lunar eclipse?
choices: The Moon turns into a star
Earth's shadow falls on the Moon
questions.fact: In a lunar eclipse, Earth sits between the Sun and the Moon and casts its shadow on the Moon.

questions.q: What happens to the sky during a total solar eclipse?
choices: It goes dark for a few minutes
questions.fact: During totality, the Moon fully covers the Sun and the sky darkens.

questions.q: How should you watch a solar eclipse?
choices: By staring straight at the Sun
questions.fact: Special eclipse glasses protect your eyes; looking straight at the Sun can hurt them.
